How the NFL season simulator works

The 2026 regular season is 18 weeks and 272 games, 17 per team. Every game that has been played keeps its real score. Every game that has not is played out 10,000 times, each time decided by that game's own home win probability: the same number the NFL Simulator gives the game at its default settings when these inputs were read, with the injury report and the game environment included. Those served win probabilities are graded game by game on the NFL Simulator.

Each simulated season also includes team strength uncertainty. Nobody knows exactly how good a team is, so every simulated season draws one strength shift per team and plays all of that team's remaining games with it: in some seasons a club is better than rated all year, in others worse. The size of that shift was fitted by replaying the 2019 to 2025 seasons from midseason, using game results and the model's own earlier probabilities, with no betting market data. Without it, the 80% win ranges held the real win total 68% to 69% of the time; with it, 78% to 81%.

Each simulated season is then seeded the way the league does it: the four division winners in each conference take seeds 1 through 4, the three best remaining records take the wild cards, and ties go through the NFL's tiebreaker steps in order.

Division title and playoff percentages on this page come from simulating the standings. Pick any remaining games yourself in the Pick the games panel above: the seeds and bracket redraw from your picks, and Run plays every season with them locked in. The NFL Playoff Simulator adds conference and Super Bowl odds and a club by club clinching check.

Tiebreakers

Head to head, division record, common games with a four game minimum, conference record, strength of victory, strength of schedule and the points based steps are all applied, in the league's order, and a tie among three or more clubs reduces to two and starts over. Best net touchdowns and the coin toss cannot be computed from the data held; a tie that reaches them stays tied rather than being settled by an invented number.

What the projection does not know

A game's probability is set by the model before kickoff. A player ruled out this week counts against his team's next game only; injured reserve and other long term absences count in every game until they end. The model does not know about an injury or a quarterback change announced after the inputs were read, and the projection is only as current as its last rebuild, stamped above in Pacific time.

NFL Season Simulator FAQ

How does the NFL season simulator work?

It plays every remaining game on the 2026 NFL schedule 10,000 times. Games already played keep their real result, every other game is decided by that game's own win probability from the TrustMyRecord NFL model, adjusted by a team strength shift drawn once per simulated season, and each simulated season is seeded with the NFL's tiebreakers.

What does the 80% range mean?

Eight of every ten simulated seasons land inside it. It shows how far a team's win total can swing on the same schedule, including the chance that the team is stronger or weaker than the model rates it. Tested on the 2019 to 2025 seasons, it covers the real win total about as often as it claims.

Which tiebreakers does it use?

Head to head, division record, common games, conference record, strength of victory, strength of schedule and the points based steps, in the league's order. Best net touchdowns and the coin toss cannot be computed from the data held, and a tie that reaches them is left tied rather than guessed.

Does it update during the season?

Yes. Each rebuild reads the schedule, every final score and the model's probabilities again, so played games stop being simulated and the ranges narrow week by week.

Is it free?

The published projection is always free to read. Your first simulation on TrustMyRecord is free, with no account needed. After that, a free account gives you one free run a day on every simulator, and each extra run costs 5 TMR. TMR Pro members run every simulator without limits. A run only counts once its result appears, so a run that fails or never finishes costs nothing.

Is this an NFL season predictor?

Yes. It is the season predictor and standings simulator for the current NFL season. It replays every remaining game and reports projected wins and division standings for all 32 teams.

Can I pick the games myself?

Yes. Pick a winner for any remaining game, week by week or one club at a time. The standings, seeds and bracket redraw from your picks with the NFL tiebreakers, Run plays every simulated season with your results locked in, and Copy link gives you a link to exactly those picks. Picking is always free; a Run counts as a simulator run.
